paper.title: Agentic World Action Models
paper.summary: Recent world action models provide visual foresight and future prediction for robot manipulation, but lack explicit mechanisms for compositional skill reuse. Agentic robotics combines code-based planning and reasoning with reusable skills, but often lacks predictive grounding in physical dynamics. We introduce AW-0, an agentic world action model framework that integrates code-based planning with joint video and action prediction. We jointly model code, future video, and robot actions as three coupled generative streams within a unified mixture-of-transformers architecture. Within this architecture a code expert generates parameterized skill routines and control logic while video and action experts generate future visual states and low-level motor commands. paper.title: When to retire: the cultural evolution of post-reproductive oblique teaching
paper.summary: Teaching is ubiquitous across human societies. Instruction from parents to offspring is the most fundamental form of teaching, explained primarily through kin selection and inclusive fitness. Instruction to non-kin, known as oblique teaching, also plays a dominant role in modern societies, where teaching is often institutionalized. Nonetheless, it remains puzzling how or when oblique teaching can evolve. Here we address the evolution of oblique teaching by developing a mathematical model of stage-structured populations. Younger individuals engage in a useful activity, called hunting, and reproduce. paper.title: Optimal galaxy magnification: generalized fundamental-plane residuals and number counts are all you need
paper.summary: Weak-lensing magnification complements cosmic shear through its effects on galaxy fluxes, sizes, and number counts. We derive the optimal magnification statistics from galaxy properties and show that the optimal measurement can be decomposed into an optimal mean statistic and total number counts. The optimal mean statistic can be constructed from the residual distribution of a generalized fundamental plane (GFP), $F(i,\boldsymbol{X})$, which predicts galaxy size or, equivalently, flux from surface brightness $i$ and additional lensing-invariant properties $\boldsymbol{X}$. The function $F$ can take any form that reduces the intrinsic scatter and thereby improves magnification precision. paper.title: LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data
paper.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) is an effective way to strengthen the long-context reasoning of large language models (LLMs), but it needs training data that are long, diverse, challenging, and verifiable. Human annotation of such data is expensive, naturally occurring data are too scarce to sustain RL, and existing synthesis methods depend on external corpora or stronger teacher models, which become harder to obtain as the trained models get stronger. Recently, RL from zero data, in which a model learns from tasks it proposes itself, has achieved excellent performance, but existing methods target short-context tasks. paper.title: Rethinking Video Autoencoders for Interactive World Models
paper.summary: Video world models predict future frames from past frames and actions. They serve as simulators in which agents train, plan or are evaluated, and that humans can control interactively. They generate in the latent space of a video autoencoder, whose compression sets their cost per frame and how long each action waits to take effect. Yet world models often reuse the autoencoders of text-to-video generators, built for offline generation with no agent waiting and, without their training data and code, not retrainable at another compression.
